messages:
maria_support: FYI customer ACME reported tool-call failures when sending timestamp fields. They get a 400 schema validation error: "expected integer—got string". Ticket #INC-3321.

alex_backend: Can you paste the request payload and the SDK used?

maria_support: Repro from customer using our hosted API + python SDK (v1.8.2):
```json
POST /v1/tools/run
{
  "tool": "schedule_meeting",
  "args": {
    "start_time": "2026-03-15T10:00:00",   // ISO string from python datetime.isoformat()
    "duration_minutes": 30
  }
}
```
Server error response: 
```json
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
{
  \"error\": \"schema_validation_failed\",
  \"details\": \"args.start_time: expected integer (epoch_ms) but got string\"
}
```

sara_py_sdk: Hmm. Python SDK's default serializer uses datetime.isoformat() for datetime objects. We usually do that for human readability, but schema for some tools expects epoch milliseconds. Did the tool schema change?

alex_backend: The tool schema was updated last week to use integer epoch_ms for clock fields to standardize across languages. Backend accepts both in theory via validation, but looks like our validator path only permits integers for this tool.

tyler_ts_sdk: TS SDK serializes Date -> number (ms since epoch) by default. That explains why TS customers didn't hit this.

raj_go_sdk: Go client currently marshals time.Time using RFC3339 string too (encoding/json default with time.Time). We might see failures for Go customers as well depending on tool schema.

maria_support: Customer repro steps: they used python SDK convenience wrapper that took a datetime and passed it through. Quick repro attached. Asking for ETA to unblock production.

nikhil_sre: Are we seeing increased 5xx or only 400s? Any rate/latency correlation?

alex_backend: Only 400s for this tool route. No latency spike. It's a serializer mismatch.

sara_py_sdk: Quick fix: add support in the SDK to serialize datetimes as epoch_ms when the request field name ends with `_time` or when a schema hint is present. But that's heuristics. Prefer adding a per-parameter serialization hint in the tool schema so SDKs can choose.

tyler_ts_sdk: We already respect schema hints if provided. Do we have a missing hint on this tool's OpenAPI spec?

alex_backend: The schema was updated but the hint flag `x-infer-epoch-ms` didn't get set due to a CI merge bug. Ops blame on me :grimacing:. I can patch server side to accept ISO strings for two releases, but long-term we should fix SDKs and republish docs.

maria_support: Customer needs an immediate workaround. They can pass `int(datetime.timestamp() * 1000)` for start_time. We told them that and they're testing.

sara_py_sdk: I'll open a hotfix PR to make python SDK accept datetime and convert to epoch_ms when generating payload for tool calls if schema expects integer. Fallback to isoformat if schema unknown. Adding unit tests + integration test against staging.

raj_go_sdk: I'll add a small helper in go-sdk to provide a `EpochMs(t time.Time)` wrapper and document it. Also add an SDK-level option `SerializeTimes: "epoch_ms|iso"` with default preserving current behavior to avoid surprise.

tyler_ts_sdk: Confirmed TS already has `timeSerialization: 'epoch'` default for compatibility. I'll add a quick note in changelog and slack the customer-facing workaround.

alex_backend: I'll also backfill the schema hint on the tool and push a tolerant validator change to accept ISO strings for two minor releases. Creating server issue: GH#redwood/infra#5472.

maria_support: Customer responds: "Workaround works, will ship for now. Please confirm permanent fix timeline."

alex_backend: Plan/ETA: backend schema hint fix + tolerant validator -> patch today (1-2h). Py SDK hotfix PR -> review today, release patch 1.8.3 tomorrow morning. Go SDK docs + opt-in helper -> end of week. Follow-up tickets: INC-3321 (customer), GH#sdk-python-220 (py hotfix), GH#infra-5472 (validator tolerance).

sara_py_sdk: Assigning myself GH#sdk-python-220. Quick note in PR: include example conversion code and add a repro integration test that posts a datetime object and asserts server receives integer epoch_ms.

nikhil_sre: I'll monitor error rates on /v1/tools/run and set an alert for >5% 400s for that tool. Linking alert -> Pager if it spikes.

maria_support: Thanks everyone. I'll update the customer with the timeline and link the PRs. :thumbsup:

alex_backend: Postmortem follow-up: need CI step to ensure `x-infer-epoch-ms` is set when schema migration runs. Adding GH#infra-5473. :memo:

sara_py_sdk: Hotfix PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/sdk-python/pull/220 - includes fallback and tests. :rocket:

maria_support: Customer confirmed workaround in prod, closing the blocking alert. Will re-open if they see issues after SDK patch. :white_check_mark:
